stories.body: Four oil tankers were reportedly damaged after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring the growing danger to commercial shipping as the conflict involving Iran escalates. The reported incidents could further disrupt a major global energy transit route.
stories.headline: Four tankers reportedly strike naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran conflict escalates

stories.body: Final or near-final results from Israel's election left neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition with the 61 Knesset seats needed to govern alone. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot won 48, while Arab-led parties secured a record combined 19 seats, making their support potentially decisive. Netanyahu's Likud has alleged foreign interference and improper support for Arab parties, claims rejected by the parties and Qatar; election officials said there was no basis for allegations of systematic violations, while Shin Bet was asked to examine reported suspicions.
stories.headline: Israel's election produces no overall majority, leaving Arab parties as potential kingmakers

stories.body: Binance said a security incident affected about $6.3 billion in digital assets, potentially making it the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. The exchange suspended deposits and withdrawals, said roughly $3 billion had been frozen or recovered with help from other platforms, and pledged to cover customer losses. Its preliminary investigation indicated that an attacker may have used access gained through a compromised engineer's laptop; blockchain intelligence firm TRM attributed the attack with high confidence to a North Korean-linked hacking unit, while Binance said it was working with law enforcement to identify those responsible.
stories.headline: Binance says a security breach affected $6.3 billion in assets in a potential record crypto heist

stories.body: China expelled a record 33 Communist Party members as its fifth plenum concluded, with party discipline taking center stage at the annual gathering. Attendance by Central Committee members and alternates fell to 279, the lowest under Xi Jinping and far below the more than 370 members named at the start of the current term in 2022. Sixteen of those expelled were military officials, including former senior figures Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli; the party gave broad allegations of serious disciplinary and legal violations, while analysts said Xi's anti-corruption campaign has also served to consolidate authority and enforce political loyalty.
stories.headline: China expels a record number of Communist Party members amid Xi Jinping's intensified purges

stories.body: North Korea tested attack drones, cruise missiles and rocket launchers during a weapons demonstration, state media reported, as Kim Jong Un called for faster development of drone and artificial-intelligence military technology. The tests follow a series of recent weapons trials and come amid heightened tensions with South Korea.
stories.headline: North Korea tests attack drones as Kim Jong Un calls for faster AI-enabled military development

stories.body: Christine Lagarde said she will leave the presidency of the European Central Bank in March, nine months before her term is due to end, saying the office's political-neutrality rules prevent her from speaking freely on broader world affairs. Her announcement followed the ECB's decision to leave its key deposit rate unchanged at 2.5% despite inflation rising to 3.8%. Lagarde's departure opens a contest for the leadership of the institution at a time of weak eurozone growth and above-target inflation, and she has been mentioned as a possible candidate to lead the World Economic Forum.
stories.headline: Christine Lagarde says she will step down early as European Central Bank president to regain freedom to speak out

stories.body: Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's supporters and Muslim community leaders in Michigan say attacks on his background by President Donald Trump, Republican nominee Mike Rogers and other Republicans have intensified anti-Muslim hostility in the closely contested race. Trump called El-Sayed a jihadist at a rally, while Rogers and allied groups have focused on alleged ties to Muslim advocacy organizations and other groups; El-Sayed has rejected those allegations and his campaign says he is focused on costs and government accountability. Dearborn officials reported an increase in threats against the city, while local advocates said the response is increased civic participation and support for El-Sayed.
stories.headline: Trump and Republican attacks on Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed raise fears of anti-Muslim backlash

stories.body: Democrats are seeking gains in rural and Republican-leaning Midwest districts as farmers and other voters contend with higher diesel, fertilizer and other input costs linked to tariffs, the war in Iran and broader market disruptions. Campaigns in Wisconsin, Minnesota and Iowa are emphasizing economic pressures and local organizing, while Republicans argue that their candidates remain better aligned with rural voters. In Arkansas, farmers are shifting acreage from rice toward less costly soybeans as expenses rise; an Arkansas agricultural economist estimated that higher costs added about $343 million for the state's farmers this year.
stories.headline: Democrats make a late push for rural Midwest districts as tariffs, energy prices and the Iran war weigh on voters

stories.body: Turning Point Action has spent about $18 million backing Republican Representative Andy Biggs in Arizona's governor's race, making the contest its largest investment and a major test of the group's influence after founder Charlie Kirk's death in 2025. Biggs, who was recruited and endorsed by Kirk, has trailed Democratic Governor Katie Hobbs in public polling, and some Arizona Republicans say the group's major spending came too late in a state where many voters cast ballots early. Turning Point says its focus is voter turnout rather than television advertising and says national Republican groups did not provide enough early support.
stories.headline: Turning Point USA's heavy investment in Arizona Republican Andy Biggs faces a pivotal test in the governor's race

stories.body: A federal judge blocked enforcement of a Trump administration rule that would have required chronically ill Medicaid recipients to prove that their conditions significantly impair their ability to meet new work requirements in order to qualify for an exemption. Judge Richard Stearns sided with 25 states and the District of Columbia, finding that they faced irreparable harm from costly changes to eligibility systems. The ruling does not invalidate the underlying work requirements, scheduled to begin in 2027 for many Medicaid expansion enrollees, but preserves a broader definition of medical frailty for exemption purposes.
stories.headline: A judge blocks the Trump administration's Medicaid rule requiring some recipients to prove impairment

stories.body: New reporting on the fatal high-speed train collision near Urda, Toledo, says controllers at Madrid's Atocha coordination center instructed the driver of a Renfe AVE train to follow the wrong protocol before it struck an Iryo train. The crash killed at least 69 people and injured dozens, while investigators and experts examine recordings of communications between the control center and train crews. Rail traffic on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed line remains suspended, Renfe has halted ticket sales through December, and authorities are continuing victim identification efforts.
stories.headline: New reporting says Atocha controllers ordered the wrong protocol before Spain's fatal Urda high-speed train collision

stories.body: Spain's high-speed rail disaster near Urda has increased political pressure on Transport Minister Óscar Puente, with opposition parties and some of the government's partners demanding accountability beyond an explanation of human error. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has continued to support Puente while promising stronger rail safety measures. The conservative Popular Party has so far emphasized mourning and calls for explanations, but is preparing to make rail infrastructure management a central issue in the coming election campaign, placing ultimate responsibility on Sánchez.
stories.headline: Spain's rail disaster deepens pressure on Transport Minister Óscar Puente as Sánchez maintains his support

stories.body: Barcelona's city government, police forces, prosecutors and courts announced heightened coordination ahead of a social-media call by Blocus-BCN for possible unrest on Saturday night. Officials said they would take preventive action and show zero tolerance for violence, looting or property damage after disturbances the previous weekend led to about 130 arrests, more than half involving minors. The authorities said they would hold legal guardians accountable where appropriate and urged families and residents to help prevent further violence.
stories.headline: Barcelona authorities announce maximum police and judicial coordination ahead of a new Blocus unrest call

stories.body: Barcelona Metro's Line 2 will be closed between La Pau and Gorg from 2 November through 3 December while Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona repairs cracks in the concrete slab supporting the tracks near Artigues-Sant Adrià. The damage was discovered after heavy early-October rains and may be related to higher groundwater levels near the Besòs River, although the operator said the link is not certain. TMB said the section remains safe but has imposed speed restrictions that caused delays and crowding, and it will operate shuttle buses and recommend metro, tram, commuter-rail and bus alternatives for the roughly 25,000 daily users affected.
stories.headline: Barcelona's Metro Line 2 will close between La Pau and Gorg for a month starting 2 November

stories.body: Catalonia's government issued an unfavorable environmental ruling on the proposed Pla de la Tallada wind farm in the Baix Empordà, citing the visual effect its four turbines would have on the Montgrí landscape. The 22.8-megawatt project had otherwise been considered viable on planning and some environmental grounds, and the wind-industry group EolicCat called the decision unprecedented and arbitrary. Local opponents welcomed the outcome but said their objections also include possible effects on nearby residents, farmland, biodiversity, migratory birds, water systems, cultural heritage and tourism; they noted that nearly 96% of voters opposed the project in a 2025 local consultation.
stories.headline: The Catalan government rejects a proposed Empordà wind farm over its landscape impact

stories.body: Sant Feliu de Guíxols has opened Walden XXI, described as Catalonia's first operating cooperative housing project specifically for older people under a right-of-use model. The conversion of the former Hotel Jecsalis created 31 homes for about 40 residents, alongside extensive shared spaces including a communal kitchen and dining room, library, laundry, workshops and outdoor areas. Residents participated in designing the project and its care arrangements, which aim to support independent community living and reduce unwanted loneliness while keeping the building in cooperative ownership for future residents.
stories.headline: Sant Feliu de Guíxols opens Catalonia's first cooperative housing project for older residents
